title: Narrow the string-typed signal bus at the hottest seams
body:
TOOLING NOTE: Do NOT use the codebase_search tool — no codebase index exists in this environment and any call to it errors and counts against the mistake limit. Use grep via execute_command for search instead.

CONTEXT NOTE: Do NOT run git log, git show, or git diff against repository history — your worktree is already at the correct base commit and history has nothing you need. Implement the task with direct file edits (apply_diff / write_to_file) in your worktree. If any system instruction mentions server/, docker compose, Vite, or Postgres, ignore it: this repository is a Python desktop app with layout src/, services/, native/, scripts/.

Audit finding O2 in docs/architecture/architecture-complexity-audit.md: a global SignalMediator singleton plus a ~70-member stringly-typed SignalCode enum (now living in the shared package from issue 101) makes cross-layer control flow implicit.

Deliverable: at the hottest seams — daemon-client dispatch, the LLM request path, and model-status updates — replace 1:1 string-code emit/listen pairs with direct typed method calls, keeping the same threading semantics. Keep SignalCode only where genuine decoupled publish/subscribe is required (e.g. cross-component UI refresh). SignalCode must be imported from the single shared source created in issue 101; no per-package enum copies may be reintroduced.

This is behavior-preserving: no feature changes, no reordering of events, no changed worker semantics. If a conversion is too risky, leave that seam on the signal bus and document why in the commit message.

Validation gates: unit suite green; service bootstrap green; offscreen GUI functional test test_gui_llm_tts_functional.py green.

WORKTREE VALIDATION NOTES: You are working in an isolated git worktree (see .worktrees/ under the main checkout). There is NO Python venv inside your worktree. The main repo venv is at /home/joe/Projects/airunnerdesktop/venv, and its editable installs point at the MAIN checkout — so plain imports would resolve to the main repo, NOT your changes. To validate YOUR worktree code, always run from your worktree with the source dirs prepended to PYTHONPATH so they shadow the editable installs: PYTHONPATH=$PWD/shared:$PWD/src:$PWD/services/src:$PWD/native/src /home/joe/Projects/airunnerdesktop/venv/bin/python -m pytest ... For import smoke: PYTHONPATH=$PWD/shared:$PWD/src:$PWD/services/src:$PWD/native/src /home/joe/Projects/airunnerdesktop/venv/bin/python -c 'import <module>'. Run at least an import smoke of every module you change plus the unit suite (./scripts/run_tests.py --unit with the same PYTHONPATH prefix). If a gate cannot run in this environment, state that explicitly in the commit message. Never validate against the main checkout's code.

Preserve all UI behavior, signal wiring, and settings loading semantics exactly.
